mechanism.rationale: The biochemistry is well characterised: TIMP1 inhibits MMPs and signals through CD63 and ITGB1. Its causal direction in ageing is unknown because MR was not tested, so the modulation direction is unclear.

evidence.value: Metalloproteinase inhibitor that functions by forming one to one complexes with target metalloproteinases, such as collagenases, and irreversibly inactivates them by binding to their catalytic zinc cofactor.
not tested: no cis instruments (p < 5e-8 within 1 Mb of the gene; 0 genome-wide). Untested is not a null result.

tractability.rationale: There is no small-molecule evidence. It is a secreted protein, so an antibody is feasible in principle, and PROTAC evidence is weak. There is no approved-drug precedence.

safety.rationale: Open Targets lists two liabilities, both generic. TIMP1 is a broad MMP inhibitor with growth-factor activity, so systemic modulation could cause off-target effects. Without MR or other data the direction of modulation is unknown.
background_knowledge: TIMP1 is pleiotropic: it inhibits many MMPs and has growth-factor and erythropoietic activity, and it is linked to cancer biology. Broad modulation may therefore have wide effects.

clinical_precedence.rationale: No drugs are listed for TIMP1.

assessment.summary: TIMP1 is a secreted MMP inhibitor with growth-factor activity. About 21% of its papers mention ageing, and it has modest associations with age-related diseases such as COPD, coronary disease and Alzheimer disease. MR could not be tested because there are no cis instruments, so causal evidence and modulation direction are missing. It has only antibody-level tractability, no clinical candidates and two generic safety liabilities. Recommendation: deprioritise.
key_uncertainties: Causal effect of the measured protein on ageing outcomes is unknown. Alternative instruments (trans pQTLs) or other causal evidence would resolve this.
